T2.id: T2-S opening dismount of infantry that start on board
T2.hypothesis: in scenarios where infantry start aboard a carrier, baseline-v2 never disembarks them (it never issues disembark), so they stay aboard for the whole game; dismounting them at the opening, while the carrier is still settled, turns them into ground units that can hold and fire
T2.trigger: at the first play decision: an own infantry aboard an own carrier (in its passengers), the carrier settled (no move path, zero speed, no stop transition), not suppressed, and disembark listed for that infantry
T2.action_change: the carrier's baseline-v2 action at that decision is replaced by the listed disembark; the carrier's MOVE is withheld until the infantry is on the ground (75 steps by Sprint 22's observed chain), then baseline-v2 drives both
T2.mechanism: disembark is listed and executed for a settled carrier (Sprint 22); the infantry is then an ordinary ground unit for baseline-v2
T2.opportunity: 74 infantry units start aboard in 10 of the 50 scenarios, none of them among the 8 frozen scenarios, so no historical capture holds an opportunity (no H0, HH or HI side)
T2.offline_analysis: none possible on the existing captures (no start-aboard infantry in any analysed game); the scenario files only show the starting passengers
T2.engine_step: one deterministic session against the inert control in a start-aboard scenario: disembark listed at the opening, executed, the carrier released, and what baseline-v2 then orders the dismounted infantry
T2.risk: the 75-step carrier hold at the opening is the withholding interaction of T2-X1 (the carrier's opening MOVE usually goes toward an unheld objective), and it cannot be measured offline because no capture holds the configuration
T2.stop: disembark not listed at the first play decision, refused, or the infantry not on the ground 75 steps after the order
T2.negative_teaches: start-aboard infantry cannot be released without a hold that baseline-v2's opening routing forbids; the infantry-defence half of T2 then needs infantry already on the ground

related_closed.T2-X1 multi-pair transport: no embark and no matching: the infantry is already aboard; the trigger is the opening state of a start-aboard scenario, the action a single disembark before the carrier first moves, not a carrier hold at a destination

T3.id: T3-O2 short memory of enemies near held objectives
T3.hypothesis: an enemy ground unit seen near a held objective within the last 300 steps but out of view now is still a threat to that objective, so a retention trigger that remembers it fires before the recapture rather than after
T3.trigger: an enemy ground unit last seen within the last 300 steps within the frozen distance of an objective the side holds, not in view now
T3.action_change: none of its own: an input of an objective-retention trigger (T13)
T3.mechanism: fewer recaptures by enemies that were out of view when the last own unit left
T3.opportunity: damage events by attackers out of view at the event but seen within 300 steps: 15 of 205 (H0) and 4 of 158 (HH); 211 disappear-and-reappear episodes in H0; how often a recapturing enemy was out of view when the objective was vacated is unpublished
T3.offline_analysis: inside the T13 loss anatomy: for each order-vacated loss, whether the capturing enemy was in view at the departure, seen within 300 steps before it, or never seen
T3.engine_step: none of its own; it would ride on a T13 probe
T3.risk: remembered phantom threats keep garrisons longer than needed
T3.stop: out-of-view capturers in fewer than one loss in four of the T13 anatomy
T3.negative_teaches: the current view is enough for objective threat; belief modelling stays unneeded at this level

related_closed.T6-G threat-entry gate: T3-O1 was to feed the T6-G gate, which never fired; T3-O2 feeds objective retention, a different trigger, and acts on no move of its own

T6.id: T6-S stacked-column stagger: offline shadow, then a two-session probe
T6.hypothesis: baseline-v2 sends co-located ground units along the same route at the same decision, so they move stacked inside visible enemies' envelopes, and the documented stacking correction favours the attacker; letting one unit go first and the others one hex time later de-stacks the column and lowers damage per exposed mover
T6.trigger: baseline-v2 emits MOVEs at this decision for two or more own ground units in the same hex whose routes share their first hex, and a visible enemy's published direct-fire range covers the movers' hex or one of the first five route hexes (Sprint 18's threat-exposed order definition)
T6.action_change: pass the MOVE of the mover with the earliest free-flow arrival; withhold each other mover's MOVE until the released unit has left the shared first hex (one hex time), then pass baseline-v2's re-proposed MOVE; at most one stagger per unit per episode; no new action type, routes unchanged
T6.mechanism: co-located movers enter each hex one hex time apart, so they are not stacked while moving through the envelope
T6.opportunity: 112 of 177 (H0) and 70 of 130 (HH) ground damage events hit a stacked victim, in 13 of 16 H0 scenario-sides; post hoc, 57 (H0) and 40 (HH) hit stacked units moving off objectives; how many of those were co-departing columns is unpublished
T6.offline_analysis: a shadow on H0 and HH with Sprint 19's envelope machinery and Sprint 23's evidence boundary: trigger episodes, units, stagger delays, stacked moving unit-steps inside envelopes on the recorded trajectories, and how many staggered units were first owners of their destination and by how much the projected delay would postpone that ownership
T6.engine_step: two head-to-head sessions in 2130511121, both seat orders: staggers executed, stacked moving unit-steps inside envelopes and damage events per exposed mover against the four HH games, first-ownership steps against HH
T6.risk: a T9-like withholding interaction, bounded to one hex time; the waiting unit stays exposed in place; the size of the stacking correction's effect on damage is not identified (Sprint 21), so the benefit is unknown before the probe
T6.stop: offline: fewer than 10 trigger episodes per HH side-game, triggers in fewer than 4 H0 scenario-sides, or a staggered unit among the first owners of its destination in more than half of the episodes; probe: stacked moving unit-steps inside envelopes not halved against HH, or any objective first owned later than in all four HH games
T6.negative_teaches: co-departing columns are not why moving units take damage, or de-stacking costs more time than it saves; the formation branch of T6 closes and route choice remains

related_closed.T6-G threat-entry gate: T6-G withheld a move entering an envelope from outside, for up to 150 steps, and never fired; T6-S acts on co-located movers already inside or entering envelopes and staggers them by one hex time
related_closed.PS-1B stalled-movement recovery: no stop action and no recovery of a formed deadlock: departures are spaced before a column forms
related_closed.T9 allocator line (T9-v1 to post-stage-a: no objective allocation, no place counting; every unit keeps its baseline-v2 destination and route

T7-C.hypothesis: a concealed unit's move (and shot) is accepted and ends concealment at once, as documented
T7-C.trigger: the deterministic P-A configuration (1910631192 C3, candidate blue against the inert control), whose concealment orders Sprint 6 reproduced exactly
T7-C.action_change: a diagnostic command, not baseline-v2 behaviour: after concealment has completed, a one-hex move for one concealed vehicle at a fixed decision; a shot from a concealed unit if one lists a target
T7-C.mechanism: the order is accepted and the unit leaves the concealed state without delay
T7-C.opportunity: the concealment trigger fires on 11 of 16 H0 scenario-sides (234 orders); but no damage event on a concealable unit in H0 and 4 in HH, and baseline-v2 orders only 1 such unit in H0 after the trigger
T7-C.offline_analysis: already done (Sprints 7 and 18): no on-policy witness and an empty benefit channel
T7-C.engine_step: one deterministic session for the move exit; the fire exit needs a configuration where a concealed unit lists a target, possibly a second session
T7-C.risk: an injected sequence baseline-v2 never produces; the result says nothing about on-policy frequency or benefit
T7-C.stop: the move is refused or concealment persists after it
T7-C.negative_teaches: exit is not free, so concealment conflicts with any later order

T8.hypothesis: changing a hovering helicopter's altitude reduces its exposure
T8.trigger: an own helicopter not moving, an enemy ground unit visible, change altitude (16) listed
T8.action_change: change altitude to a listed level (an action type baseline-v2 never issues)
T8.mechanism: different altitude, different observation and damage modifiers
T8.opportunity: change altitude listed in 6,957 H0 decisions; altitude, fortification or mine-laying listed on 4 of 16 H0 scenario-sides; 13 aircraft damage events in H0, none while moving, on 4 of 16 H0 scenario-sides
T8.engine_step: one deterministic session for the transition; the exposure effect needs two head-to-head sessions
T8.risk: the altitude effect is documented for transport helicopters, not for attack helicopters
T8.stop: the transition is refused or changes neither observation nor damage
T8.negative_teaches: altitude does not protect attack helicopters

T10.hypothesis: action 7 issued to a suppressed own infantry unit ends its suppression early and restores movement and fire, and avoids the documented squad loss on re-suppression
T10.trigger: an own infantry unit with keep 1 and action 7 listed
T10.action_change: issue the listed remove-suppression (an action type baseline-v2 never issues, to a unit baseline-v2 cannot command while suppressed)
T10.mechanism: keep returns to 0 (at once or after a delay); move and shoot are listed again
T10.opportunity: infantry suppression onsets 15 (H0, 6 of 16 scenario-sides) and 4 (HH); remove suppression listed in 1,709 H0 unit-decisions, all while suppressed; post hoc, already suppressed infantry lost a squad outside damage in 25 of 25 cases
T10.engine_step: head-to-head sessions in a configuration with infantry suppression, an add-on that changes no baseline-v2 action
T10.risk: an undocumented cost of the action; suppression of infantry is rare (about one onset per H0 side-game), so the sessions may produce few events
T10.stop: refused, or keep unchanged after the order
T10.negative_teaches: the action is useless; the family closes

T12.id: T12-O1 objective-zone dispersion: offline count, then one deterministic and two head-to-head sessions
T12.hypothesis: moving all but one stacked holder of a held objective to free adjacent hexes keeps the objective denied and removes the stacked-target correction
T12.trigger: a held objective with two or more idle own ground units on its hex and a passable adjacent hex with fewer than four own ground units
T12.action_change: a one-hex move for each extra unit; baseline-v2's later moves for dispersed units withheld while the objective is held
T12.mechanism: stack cleared, objective still held, fewer damage events on holders
T12.opportunity: post hoc, stationary stacked units on objectives took 40 (H0, on 10 of 16 scenario-sides) and 10 (HH) ground damage events; but baseline-v2 moves a vehicle on from a held objective at once in most corpus arrivals, so idle stacked holders may be rare
T12.offline_analysis: trigger occurrences, timing, adjacency and passability on H0 and HH, and the claimant measure for the dispersed units' withheld moves
T12.engine_step: one deterministic session for execution, then two head-to-head sessions for denial and damage
T12.risk: the withholding interaction of T9 and T2-X1; adjacent denial is documented but untested
T12.stop: offline: fewer than one trigger per side-game; probe: an objective captured while a dispersed holder stands next to it
T12.negative_teaches: only on-hex holding denies capture, or holders rarely stack idle under baseline-v2

related_closed.T9 allocator line (T9-v1 to post-stage-a: no capacity allocation among claimants: only units already holding a captured objective are moved, one hex, inside its denial zone

T13.id: T13-D1 held-objective loss anatomy and garrison shadow (offline), then a two-session garrison probe
T13.hypothesis: held objectives are lost mainly because baseline-v2 orders the last own ground unit out of the objective's denial zone (its hex and six neighbours) while an enemy can still reach it; keeping that unit in the zone while a visible enemy ground unit is near denies the recapture by the documented capture rule, at the cost of the unit's onward move
T13.trigger: at a play decision: an objective the side holds; exactly one own ground unit (not artillery, not aboard) in its denial zone; baseline-v2 emits a MOVE for that unit whose route leaves the zone; a visible enemy ground unit within a frozen distance of the objective (proposed: the largest published direct-fire range plus one hex, fixed in the experiment's registration)
T13.action_change: withhold that MOVE for this decision (baseline-v2 re-proposes it at the next); the hold ends when another own ground unit is in the zone, no visible enemy ground unit is within the distance, or a frozen bound expires (proposed 300 steps); no new action type, routes unchanged
T13.mechanism: by the capture rule an enemy cannot occupy while an own ground unit is in the zone, and no held-objective loss in H0 or HH occurred with an own unit on the hex; the offline step tests whether losses follow order-vacating rather than destruction, and what the hold would cost in onward captures
T13.opportunity: 40 losses of held objectives in H0 on 7 of 16 scenario-sides and 26 in the 4 HH side-games (25 first ownerships there), none with an own unit on the hex before; baseline-v2 sends vehicles on from held objectives at once (107 of 155 corpus arrivals); how many losses followed an order rather than a destruction is unpublished
T13.offline_analysis: a registered diagnostic on H0 (16 scenario-sides) and HH (4 side-games, 2 distinct openings) through the existing census pipeline, no engine: for each held-objective loss, the last own ground unit to leave the denial zone before the enemy's occupation, classified V-ORDER (left alive under a baseline-v2 MOVE), V-LOSS (destroyed in the zone) or V-OTHER; for V-ORDER, the steps from departure to loss, the nearest visible enemy ground unit at departure, the departing unit's next destination (held or unheld) and whether it was among the first owners there; the frozen garrison rule as a first-divergence shadow with certificates (Sprint 23's evidence boundary); counts by game, scenario-side, distinct setup, opportunity and unit
T13.engine_step: two head-to-head sessions in 2130511121 (the HH configuration), the garrison add-on on baseline-v2 in each seat order against baseline-v2, mechanism endpoints only: garrison episodes and holds, losses of a garrisoned objective while the garrison lives in the zone (none expected by rule), losses after release or destruction of the garrison, garrison losses, first-ownership steps against the four HH games, withheld moves
T13.risk: the withholding interaction that shelved T9 and T2-X1: the last unit in a held zone is usually one baseline-v2 sends on to an unheld objective; a stationary garrison may be destroyed in place (post hoc, stationary units on objectives took 13 alone and 40 stacked of the 177 H0 ground damage events)
T13.stop: offline: V-ORDER in fewer than half of the losses; fewer than 4 losses the shadow would have touched, or touched losses on fewer than 2 scenario-sides; or the departing unit among the first owners of its next objective in more than half of the V-ORDER losses: then no engine step. Probe: a garrisoned objective lost while the garrison lives in the zone, garrisons destroyed in half or more of the episodes with an enemy approach, or any objective first owned later than in all four HH games
T13.negative_teaches: losses of held objectives come from destruction or from situations one garrison cannot cover, so retention needs fire or formation rather than holding; or the onward moves are worth more than retention, which bounds every hold-type tactic on baseline-v2

related_closed.T2-X1 multi-pair transport: no transport and no carrier: the hold is the tactic itself (denial of a held objective), not the overhead of a delivery; its cost is measured first, offline
related_closed.T9 allocator line (T9-v1 to post-stage-a: no allocation of claimants to objectives and no place counting: only the departure of the last unit from an objective already held is withheld, while an enemy is near
related_closed.T6-G threat-entry gate: T6-G withheld a move into an envelope; T13 withholds a move away from a held objective, for its denial

T13.name: objective retention (post-capture denial): keep the last own ground unit in a held objective's denial zone while a visible enemy ground unit is near

not_admitted.infantry tactical positioning (hold infa: condition 6: withholding a claimant that cannot arrive before the end restates the T9 batch allocator's rule that such a claimant is never seated (Sprint 11)
not_admitted.deterministic fire allocation without a: conditions 4 and 7: a target rule's benefit runs through kills, whose probability law is unidentified (Sprint 21), or through objective retention that only a scored comparison shows; suppression does not stop a capture (the rules let a suppressed unit occupy)
not_admitted.local movement congestion prevention: condition 6: its target is the deadlock the PS-1 study diagnosed (10 deadlock episodes in the 8-game corpus, post hoc); PS-1 is shelved and its problem is reopened only with the owner's approval; T6-S's spacing of co-departing columns is scored for exposure, not as a deadlock remedy

not_admitted.close-combat avoidance: Sprint 18's reason stands (a route-entry case of T6), and condition 4: close combat is a two-sided exchange whose net effect is unmeasured below the score
